assumptions: Request volume is assumed flat at the 200 flag evaluations per minute reported in the logs; no independent traffic metric was consulted.

Customer-facing impact is assumed to run from the flag flip at 21:30 to the revert at 21:37 (~7 minutes). The incident record's 0.02 hours covers only alert-to-resolution (21:35:42-21:37:07) and understates the time customers saw errors; the alert fired about five minutes after errors began.
The reported error rate of -1.7% is negative and therefore not usable as stated; the per-minute log figures (0-2% baseline rising to 31-34%) were used instead to characterise severity.

The 20:19 onset referenced in the alternative hypothesis was not corroborated by any log line in the window supplied and is assumed to belong to the pre-existing payment-authorisation timeouts rather than to this incident.
Assumed the account page is reachable by signed-in customers generally rather than a small internal or admin audience; no traffic-composition data was available.

The ZeroDivisionError is assumed to be a latent defect in the flagged code path rather than something introduced alongside the flag flip, since no deploy was recorded between 18:00 and 21:36. The actual denominator that reached zero was not identified from the logs.
input.executive_summary: On 2 September 2026, roughly a third of visits to the customer account page failed with an error for about seven minutes (21:30-21:37 UTC). The cause was a newly switched-on internal setting that enabled an unfinished monthly-spend display; the code behind it crashed whenever it had nothing to divide by. Customers who hit it saw an error instead of their account page; other parts of the shop, including buying, were unaffected. The setting was switched back off and the page recovered immediately. A small, pre-existing trickle of payment-authorisation timeouts (0-2% of requests) was present before, during and after the incident and is a separate, ongoing issue.
input.impact_weight_reason: Every failing request in the logs is an account-page render, and the failing code is an account-page display of monthly spend — not a cart, checkout or payment submission path, and nothing in the evidence shows a purchase being attempted or lost. It is not zero, though: the account page sits inside the logged-in purchase funnel and the same handler makes payment-authorisation calls (the UpstreamTimeout lines), so some customers who bounced off an error page would plausibly have gone on to buy, and most of the rest would have returned given the seven-minute duration. 0.15 reflects "signed-in page adjacent to buying, but not the buying step itself." This is a judgement from log paths only; no session, funnel or conversion data was available to check what fraction of account-page visitors convert.
input.root_cause: The feature flag `monthly-spend-feature` was enabled, and the account-page code path it gates performs a division whose denominator can be zero (ZeroDivisionError), so every request that evaluated the flag as "on" returned an error. Logs show the flag move from `off` (200/200 evaluations) to a partial split at 21:30 (143 off / 57 on) to fully `on` at 21:31, with the account-page error rate tracking it exactly: ~0-2% baseline, then 8%, then 31-34%. No deploy or other change was recorded between 18:00 and 21:36. Turning the flag off returned the service to baseline, confirming the cause.
